app_documentation:
The Hospital Appointment Booking System is a modern, patient-centric healthcare application designed to streamline the appointment scheduling process between patients and doctors. Built as a cross-platform solution for both web and mobile devices using React, Node.js, Express, and TypeScript with a PostgreSQL database, the system serves as a comprehensive digital platform that eliminates traditional barriers in healthcare access. The application enables patients to easily register, search for doctors by specialization, view real-time availability, and book appointments at their convenience, while providing doctors with efficient tools to manage their schedules and patient interactions.

The system's core features include Patient Registration (F1) allowing users to create and manage their accounts with personal details, Appointment Booking (F2) enabling patients to view available doctor slots and schedule visits, Doctor Schedule Management (F3) providing doctors the ability to set availability and view scheduled appointments, Appointment Cancellation and Rescheduling (F4) offering flexibility for both patients and doctors to modify bookings, and Notifications and Reminders (F5) delivering automated email and SMS communications to reduce no-shows and keep all parties informed. The application implements a clean, medical-professional aesthetic with calming colors, intuitive navigation through a bottom navigation bar, and accessibility features compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA standards.

The intended users span three primary roles: Patients who need to book and manage medical appointments, Doctors who require tools to manage their availability and view patient schedules, and Administrators who oversee system operations. The system architecture ensures data integrity through proper database relationships, implements security best practices including bcrypt password hashing, and maintains performance through strategic indexing on frequently queried columns. With features like real-time slot availability checking, conflict prevention for double-bookings, 24-hour appointment reminders, and comprehensive appointment history tracking, the Hospital Appointment Booking System represents a complete solution for modern healthcare appointment management.

The technical implementation leverages a RESTful API architecture with TypeScript for type safety, PostgreSQL for robust data storage with UUID primary keys and proper foreign key relationships, and a responsive React frontend optimized for mobile-first experiences. The system stores all timestamps in UTC, supports both email and SMS notification channels, and implements proper transaction handling to prevent booking conflicts. The database schema includes six core tables (users, patients, doctors, availability_slots, appointments, notifications) with carefully designed relationships and indexes to ensure optimal query performance and data consistency across the platform.

glossary.Availability Slot: A specific time period defined by a doctor during which they are available to see patients. Each slot has a start time, end time, date, and availability status. Slots are typically 30 minutes in duration and can be booked by only one patient at a time.
glossary.Appointment Status: The current state of a scheduled appointment, which can be one of four values: 'scheduled' (confirmed and upcoming), 'completed' (patient visit finished), 'cancelled' (appointment terminated by patient or doctor), or 'rescheduled' (moved to a different time slot).
glossary.User Role: The classification of a system user that determines their permissions and available features. The three roles are: Patient (can book and manage appointments), Doctor (can set availability and view patient schedules), and Administrator (can oversee system operations).
glossary.Notification Channel: The communication medium through which the system sends messages to users. Supported channels include email (electronic mail), SMS (text message to mobile phone), and push (in-app notification). Each notification is sent through one or more channels based on user preferences.
glossary.Slot Conflict: A situation where multiple users attempt to book the same availability slot simultaneously, or when a booking request is made for a slot that is no longer available. The system prevents conflicts through transaction handling and real-time availability checking.
glossary.Baseline Artifact: A formally approved and version-controlled project document that serves as a reference point for the current state of requirements, design, or architecture. Changes to baseline artifacts require formal change management and version increment.
